section_summary: This section documents the administrative and legal implementation of postwar Japanese rural land reform, focusing particularly on the expropriation of Japanese agricultural land held by absentee landlords residing abroad. It includes Japanese statutory texts, imperial ordinances, and enforcement regulations, as well as diplomatic correspondence between the Department of State, the Japanese American Citizens League, the Swedish diplomatic mission representing Japanese interests, and the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It also features detailed GHQ SCAP legal studies examining whether compulsorily acquiring farmland owned by American and Allied citizens against payment in depreciated, non-convertible yen constitutes illegal confiscation under international law.

subfiles.about: Compendium of Japanese statutes, imperial ordinances, and administrative regulations governing rural land reform and agricultural land commissions.
subfiles.from: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and Rural Self-Rule Association
subfiles.summary: A published Japanese legal compendium on rural land reform issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and the Rural Self-Rule Association. This segment includes the table of contents and full texts of the Agricultural Land Adjustment Law (as amended October 1946), its Enforcement Ordinance (Imperial Ordinance No. 38, as amended by Imperial Ordinance No. 556), and Enforcement Regulations (MAF Ordinance No. 4, as amended by MAF Ordinance No. 68). The legislation regulates tenancy conditions, restricts agricultural land transfers, creates municipal and prefectural agricultural land commissions, and provides administrative procedures for establishing owner-cultivators.
subfiles.title: Laws and Regulations Relating to the Reform of the Agricultural Land System and Explanation Thereof

subfiles.about: Transmitting diplomatic correspondence between the Swedish Diplomatic Mission and the Japanese Foreign Office regarding the application of Japanese rural land reform to Japanese nationals residing abroad.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding diplomatic correspondence between the Swedish Diplomatic Mission and the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning whether farm land purchases can be postponed for Japanese nationals living abroad, particularly in Hawaii. The Japanese government clarifies that agricultural lands owned by non-residents must be compulsorily purchased without exception for foreign residence, though owners or custodians may file statements with local agricultural land commissions. Enclosures include Swedish inquiries, Japanese diplomatic notes, a Foreign Ministry explanatory memorandum detailing purchase standards and 30-year bond terms, and SCAP's December 1945 rural land reform directive.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1118: Application of Japanese Rural Land Reform Measures to Japanese Subjects Residing Abroad

subfiles.about: Transmitting GHQ SCAP check sheets concerning the legal and administrative applicability of Japanese land reform expropriation to farmland owned by American citizens.
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting GHQ SCAP check sheets regarding whether Japanese agrarian reform measures apply to agricultural land in Japan owned by American citizens. A Legal Section opinion concludes that expropriation compensated only in depreciated, non-convertible yen constitutes illegal confiscation under international law, recommending exemption for pre-enactment titles unless prompt, adequate, and effective compensation is provided. A Natural Resources Section study summarizes land purchase thresholds, opposes exceptional treatment for transfers to Allied nationals after promulgation, and addresses the farmland holdings of George Tsutsui.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 411: Application of Japanese Agrarian Land Reform Measures to Property of American Citizens
